The change under review adds a uv binary download to every CI job without using the integrity control the pinned action offers. The action's own recorded execution states "Checksum not provided. Checking known checksums." and "No known checksum found for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl-0.13.1" (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-uv-action.json:11), so in an actual run uv is fetched from GitHub releases with no digest verification; the pinned v6.6.0 manifest predates uv 0.13.1, so its known-checksum table cannot cover the pinned version on any platform. .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:45-50 passes only version/enable-cache/github-token even though the manifest declares a `checksum` input (.local/ci-bootstrap-2026-10-17/setup-uv-repository/action.yml:21-23), and the owned bootstrap only compares `uv --version` text, not the binary. The authoritative digests are already in the repository's own evidence (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-python-bootstrap.json:8-13 records archiveSha256 6c86040a… verified against the astral-sh/uv release API and binarySha256 752a98d0…), and docs/checks/phase-08-ci-uv-action.json:23 only asserts the match for the local exercise. docs/CI.md:54-62 discusses this residual trust for rustup but never states that the CI uv acquisition itself is unverified, while docs/phase-status.json:696 says the bootstrap used "hash-verified official uv 0.13.1", which is true only of the local run and is easy to read as covering CI.
